Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The Smart ID card supports digital authentication. The eHomeAffairs portal uses OTP authentication linked to the ID number. HANIS enables fingerprint-based authentication. The DHA's Online Verification Service (OVS) is used by government departments and banks for real-time identity verification (180,000+ daily transactions). The MyMzansi roadmap launched a functional Digital ID with remote authentication capability in Q4 2025. MTN deployed nationwide biometric authentication using Home Affairs integration.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: The eHomeAffairs portal (ehome.dha.gov.za) allows authenticated access using the South African ID number and OTP sent to registered cellphone. Citizens can apply for Smart IDs and passports online. The eservices.gov.za site provides access to 194+ government e-services. The MyMzansi platform is being built as a single government portal with digital ID authentication. Government portal authentication via Smart ID is operational but not yet fully unified.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: POPIA gives South African citizens nine data rights including the right to access, correct, and request deletion of their personal information. The Promotion of Access to Information Act (PAIA) 2000 provides a formal mechanism to request personal data held by government. The Identification Act Section 19 provides for correction of ID documentation. The MyMzansi roadmap plans a Credentials Wallet allowing citizens to view and share verified data. Citizens currently can access their data through formal PAIA/POPIA processes.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: South Africa's Smart ID and HANIS database are used for KYC by financial institutions under FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act). Banks verify customer identity against the Home Affairs National Identification System. The DHA OVS provides real-time identity verification to banks. SASSA uses DHA database cross-checks for grant beneficiary KYC without requiring applicants to submit documentation. Private ID verification companies (VerifyNow, iiDENTIFii) offer API-based KYC against Home Affairs records.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: South Africa has general judicial oversight through its constitutional courts and the Promotion of Access to Information Act (PAIA) 2000, which allows individuals to challenge government data handling. The Information Regulator (IRSA) provides quasi-judicial oversight of data protection. However, there are no ID-system-specific judicial mechanisms. Courts can adjudicate ID-related disputes but no dedicated ID court or tribunal exists.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Birth registration is linked to the National Population Register and is a prerequisite for obtaining an ID number. The DHA has rolled out online birth registration to 161 health facilities, targeting all 1,445 public maternity wards. Early Birth Registration (within 30 days) is promoted. However, integration is partial: the DHA December 2025 white paper proposes an Intelligent Population Register (IPR) to make birth registration mandatory via digital channels, indicating current integration is not yet fully complete. NISIS remains undeveloped.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing is partially governed. The Identification Act Section 21 restricts unauthorized access to the NPR, with the Director-General able to approve access for specific purposes. POPIA establishes lawful processing conditions for data sharing. The DHA OIM Policy 2022 acknowledges that rule-based access governed by legislation is the goal, but notes current challenges with ad-hoc 'data dumping' to other government systems contrary to POPIA. Data sharing rules partially available/partially implemented.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No enacted digital-ID-specific regulation as of 2025. The National Identification and Registration Bill 2023 was gazetted for comment in April 2023 and revised, but had not been submitted to Cabinet or enacted as of 2025. President Ramaphosa confirmed in February 2026 that the legal framework was still pending Cabinet approval. The MyMzansi roadmap identifies digital ID as a 2025/26 initiative but legislation remains outstanding.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), Act 4 of 2013, came into full effect on 1 July 2021. It establishes eight conditions for lawful data processing, nine rights for data subjects, and the Information Regulator of South Africa (IRSA) as the enforcement authority. POPIA applies to both public and private bodies processing personal information in South Africa, including identity management systems.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Information Regulator of South Africa (IRSA) was established under POPIA and became operational in 2021. It has broad powers including issuing enforcement notices, conducting investigations, imposing fines up to ZAR 10 million, and receiving complaints from individuals. In April 2025 the IRSA launched a mandatory e-portal for data breach reporting, demonstrating active enforcement. The IRSA has issued enforcement notices to Dis-Chem and SAPS.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The Smart ID card is the official government-issued identity document and constitutes legal proof of identity in South Africa. It is required for registering for matric exams, applying for a driver's license, opening a bank account, accessing social grants, and voting. The Official Identity Management Policy (Cabinet-approved March 2022) positions the DHA as the sole provider of official legal identity documents for citizens and lawful residents.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A comprehensive legal framework governs South Africa's ID system. Key legislation includes the Identification Act 68 of 1997, the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1992, the Citizenship Act, and the Constitution (Section 28). The Official Identity Management Policy was Cabinet-approved in March 2022. The National Identification and Registration Bill 2023 was gazetted for public comment. POPIA (2013, in force 2021) and PAIA 2000 also govern the framework.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: South Africa's ID system maintenance is a mix of in-country and foreign vendors. NEC Corporation (Japan) provided and maintains the HANIS AFIS system. IDEMIA (France) has a 10-year contract for Smart ID card production and biometric enrollment. However, the DHA has collaborated with local engineers and SITA (State IT Agency). The DHA strategic plan explicitly notes dependency on third parties for critical services. Partial in-country maintenance capacity exists alongside dominant foreign vendor involvement.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Department of Home Affairs (DHA) is subject to oversight by National Treasury under the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA) 1999 and Treasury Regulations. National Treasury created the self-financing mechanism for Smart ID production costs. The DHA Strategic Plan 2025-30 explicitly references PFMA oversight and Treasury-approved budget frameworks. However, there is no dedicated Ministry of Finance role specifically for the ID system; oversight is through the general government fiscal framework. Classified as partial.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The DHA ID system is primarily domestically funded. The DHA 2025/26 budget is R11 billion, drawn from the national government budget. National Treasury created a self-financing mechanism where DHA retains revenue from document fees. No significant external/donor funding for the core ID system was identified. The DHA 2025-30 Strategic Plan notes the department is 'grossly underfunded' but relies on domestic public funds, not external donors, for core operations.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: South Africa's HANIS (Home Affairs National Identification System) collects fingerprints as the primary biometric. The Smart ID card stores fingerprints and facial recognition data. The ABIS (Automated Biometric Identification System) upgrade adds iris and palm print capabilities. The 2025/26 DHA budget speech confirmed facial recognition as the primary biometric for the new digital identity system. Biometric modalities thus include fingerprints and facial/iris, qualifying as Facial/Iris category.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The National Population Register (NPR) and HANIS are fully digital systems. The DHA's ABIS and live capture systems are digital. A major digitisation project is underway to convert over 340 million paper-based civic records to digital; over 49 million records digitised as of mid-2025. While legacy paper records remain, the active identity database is fully digital.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The DHA's Online Verification Service (OVS) allows some government departments and private banks to query the population register. The upgraded digital ID verification service handles over 180,000 transactions daily and is used by SASSA, SAPS, and Department of Justice, plus three private-sector entities. However, full interoperability is fragmented: the National Integrated Social Information System (NISIS) remains undeveloped, data is siloed across departments, and the DHA draft policy explicitly acknowledges interoperability challenges. Partial interoperability exists.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: South African financial institutions require identity verification under FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act). The Smart ID card or green ID book is accepted for opening bank accounts, and FICA requires KYC using these documents. However, use of Smart ID is accepted but not exclusively mandatory (passports and other documents are also accepted for FICA). The DHA/banking partnership enables Smart ID applications at 30+ bank branches. ID is accepted (not exclusively mandatory) for banking.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: Smart ID issuance is free for first-time applicants who are 16 years old (youth). It is also free for pensioners (60 years and above). However, replacement Smart IDs for lost/stolen documents cost R140. Older citizens replacing green ID books with Smart IDs may also face fees. While free for first-time youth applicants, a cost applies in many cases. Coded as 'Yes' (cost exists for some).

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: South Africa participated in a successful pilot with Lesotho for real-time cross-border digital identity verification, enabling Lesotho migrants to access remittance services in South Africa using their national digital IDs. In August 2025, a SADC regional DPI initiative was launched to build Africa's first cross-border digital identity framework across 16 SADC member states. Recognition is at the regional pilot/framework stage, not yet formally interoperable at scale. Classified as 'Some regional' recognition.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Current law (Identification Act) requires citizens aged 16 and above to apply for an ID. The DHA requirements confirm 'FIRST TIME ISSUANCE OF A SMART ID CARD: YOUTH WHO ARE 16 YEARS AND ABOVE.' The Official Identity Management Policy (2022) proposes lowering the enrollment age to 10 years, and the National Identification Registration Bill 2023 includes this provision, but it has not yet been enacted. Current eligibility age is 16 (>17 bracket = value 1 as per scale, noting 16 rounds to >17 scale).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The Identification Act 68 of 1997 mandates that all South African citizens aged 16 and above must apply for an identity document within 7 days of a request by an authorized official, with failure to apply being a criminal offense (fine or up to 12 months imprisonment per GNR.978 of 1998). All persons required to have an ID must surrender green ID books when issued a Smart ID. Enrollment is effectively mandatory for all eligible citizens.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: ID is accepted for healthcare access in South Africa. The DHA Draft OIM Policy (2020) identified the Department of Health as a major customer of the National Identity System. The SASSA biometric system for grant payments (which includes healthcare grants) requires ID. However, public healthcare in South Africa is generally accessible without mandatory ID, though ID facilitates enrollment in health programs. ID is accepted but not universally mandatory for basic healthcare access.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Permanent residents (from visa-exempt countries) became eligible for Smart ID cards from May 2025, covering ~1.4 million people. Citizens by naturalization were also included from May 2025. However, temporary residents, asylum seekers, and other non-nationals are not eligible for the Smart ID (they use separate permits/documentation). HANIS/ABIS stores biometrics for all non-citizens including refugees and asylum seekers. Some non-nationals are thus included.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Over 25 million Smart ID cards issued by end of 2024/25 (as confirmed in DHA speech). Additionally, older green bar-coded ID books are held by tens of millions more citizens. South Africa's total population is approximately 62 million (2025), with ~40-42 million adults 16+. The NPR covers effectively all citizens. Combining Smart IDs (~25 million) and green ID books still in use, coverage of the eligible adult population exceeds 70-80%, placing South Africa in the 70-89% bracket. The MyMzansi roadmap targets 90% Smart ID uptake by 2028.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: The South African Auditor-General has conducted reviews of DHA systems, including a report flagging 'brazen corruption' in the ABIS tender process (2020), which led to the tender being declared irregular. POPIA mandates Personal Information Impact Assessments for public bodies. The DHA 2023/24 Annual Report indicates security and compliance oversight. The upgraded OVS system undergoes performance monitoring. Security reviews exist but are general government audit processes rather than dedicated ID-specific security audits.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration is mandatory in South Africa under the Regulation of Interception of Communications and Provision of Communication-Related Information Act (RICA) 2002, effective 2009. All new prepaid and contract SIM cards must be registered with a government-issued ID (SA ID book or card, passport for foreigners) and proof of residence before activation. Network operators cannot activate a SIM without RICA registration. ID use for SIM registration is mandatory.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: A South African ID number is mandatory for receiving SASSA social grants. Grant eligibility is verified by cross-checking the ID number against Home Affairs records. From September 2025, SASSA implemented mandatory biometric enrollment for all grant beneficiaries. The Child Support Grant requires ID registration as a prerequisite. Undocumented citizens cannot access grants. ID use for social services is mandatory.
